sum: Equinor faced two investor-relevant developments during the week of November 9 to 13, 2026. On Friday, November 13, the company's shares began trading on the Oslo Stock Exchange without entitlement to the second-quarter cash dividend, according to Equinor.

The cash distribution amounts to 0.39 US dollars per share. The ex-dividend date separates the entitlement to the payment from shares bought afterward and puts shareholder returns alongside operating developments in the weekly investor view.

On November 9, crews were preparing repairs at Equinor's Visund gas and oil platform after a fire in an electrical system halted production earlier in the week, Intelatus Global Partners reported, citing Reuters and an Equinor spokesperson.

The platform was scheduled to remain offline until November 16, although the timetable could change. Thirty-six people remained on board for logistical work and site security, compared with 128 at the time of the incident. Gassco estimates Visund's output capacity at 13.2 million cubic metres of natural gas per day, equivalent to about 3.7 percent of Norway's export capacity.

For investors, the dividend milestone provides a defined cash-return date, while the Visund outage keeps operational execution in view. The repair schedule and the timing of a production restart are the next practical markers for the affected asset.

sum: Equinor's Wisting development moved into a new engineering phase on Monday, November 9, 2026, after Kongsberg Maritime won an initial contract for safety and automation systems on the planned floating production, storage and offloading vessel. The Maritime Executive reported the award in a publication dated November 9, citing a release from Kongsberg Maritime.

The contract covers front-end engineering and design for the FPSO's Safety and Automation System. Kongsberg will work with Equinor and other project suppliers to develop and mature a concept intended to support a safe, efficient and sanctionable development.

The initial scope is focused on technical work rather than production. It includes the design of automation and safety solutions for the vessel and allows Kongsberg to bring its offshore engineering and digital capabilities into the project at an early stage.

Wisting is located in the Barents Sea, approximately 300 kilometers north of mainland Norway. Kongsberg's release described the field as one of the larger undeveloped oil discoveries on the Norwegian Continental Shelf and said the project could have an anticipated operating life of around 30 years.

The contract does not represent a final investment decision, a production start or a completed construction award. If Wisting advances into the execution phase, Kongsberg's potential scope could expand to process control, safety systems, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity across the FPSO's lifecycle.

Neither the contract value nor a delivery timetable was disclosed. For Equinor investors, the immediate significance is that technical preparation is progressing, while the larger development decision and any future capital commitment remain ahead. The early engineering work can improve project definition, but it does not yet establish a firm production schedule or project economics.

Kongsberg Maritime President and CEO Lisa Edvardsen Haugan said the company viewed Wisting as an important addition to its offshore energy portfolio. She also highlighted automation, safety, digitalisation and cybersecurity as areas in which Kongsberg expects to contribute to the FPSO concept.

sum: Equinor's third-quarter 2026 report landed on 28 October with an adjusted operating profit of USD 12.35 billion, helped along by higher production volumes and firmer oil and gas prices, according to Reuters. Net profit came in at USD 2.54 billion, while adjusted net income reached USD 2.86 billion.

The Norwegian energy major used the quarterly release to lift its full-year 2026 oil and gas output growth forecast to around 4%, up from 3% previously. Adjusted earnings per share for the quarter stood at USD 1.20, and the company declared a dividend of USD 0.39 per share.

Shareholder returns extend beyond the dividend. Buybacks are set to total up to USD 3 billion across the year, a figure that includes shares repurchased from the Norwegian state for cancellation. Roughly two weeks before the results, Equinor announced the fourth and final tranche of its 2026 repurchase programme, worth up to USD 1.125 million, of which up to USD 371.3 million is earmarked for on-market purchases. Production capacity at Visund remains shut in following a fire in an electrical facility. The platform is still down while repair work is being prepared, and a Gassco schedule pointed to a possible restart on 16 November — a date explicitly subject to change. Visund can deliver 13.2 million cubic metres of gas per day.

Norway's safety regulator Havtil opened an investigation into the blaze on Wednesday, focusing on the emergency power switchgear room. The Equinor-operated facility was shut down and depressurised, and no injuries were reported. Crews on board have been reduced to 36 people, down from 128 at the time of the incident.

Wednesday brought pressure from the crude market. Brent fell 8% and settled at a two-month low, Reuters reported, after results from the US midterm elections stoked hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war and of higher crude exports from the Middle East.

Equinor stock faces Visund outage after North Sea platform fire
sum: Equinor halted production at its Visund platform in the Norwegian North Sea on Wednesday, November 4, after a fire in an electrical switchboard room. Winda Beacon reported that the fire was extinguished by mid-afternoon, no injuries were reported and about 70 of the 128 people on board were moved to other installations or shore.

Equinor spokesperson Ellen Maria Skjelsbaek said repairs would be needed and that it was too early to give a restart date, according to the report. The company reported the incident to the authorities, while the cause and the extent of damage to the electrical systems remained undisclosed.

Gassco reduced Visund's available export capacity to 2.5 million cubic meters per day from 12:53 CET on November 4 and to zero for the November 5 gas day. The platform's full capacity is 13.2 million cubic meters per day. Gas from Visund moves through the Kvitebjorn pipeline to the Kollsnes processing plant before reaching European markets.

The interruption came alongside unplanned reductions at other Norwegian fields, including Asgard, Oseberg and Troll. Gassco's November 4 export nominations stood at 324.8 million cubic meters at 17:03 CET, according to the report. That places Visund's full export capacity at roughly 4 percent of that day's nominations, although the commercial impact will depend mainly on how long the shutdown lasts.
Visund has produced since 1999 and is mainly a gas field. Equinor operates the asset with a 53.2 percent interest. Petoro holds 30 percent, ConocoPhillips 9.1 percent and Repsol 7.7 percent.

The immediate issue for Equinor is the repair timetable. A short interruption would mainly affect near-term production and export volumes, while a prolonged outage could increase operational pressure in a period when several Norwegian fields have reported unplanned reductions. No restart date has been announced, so further updates from Equinor and Gassco are the next material signals.

sum: Equinor reported stronger third-quarter operating performance on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and raised its full-year production outlook. The company said adjusted operating income reached USD 12.35 billion, while adjusted net income was USD 2.86 billion. The figures were published in the company's third-quarter results release.

Equity production rose 2 percent year over year to 2,166 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. International oil and gas output increased 21 percent, helped by production from Adura in the United Kingdom and Bacalhau in Brazil and by lower turnaround activity. Production on the Norwegian continental shelf was stable, while US production declined from the year-earlier quarter.

Equinor raised its 2026 oil and gas production growth guidance from 3 percent to around 4 percent. Chief Executive Anders Opedal said strong production, higher prices and safe operations supported the change. The company also pointed to a record contribution from the Mongstad refinery and strong Marketing, Midstream and Processing results.

Cash flow from operations after taxes paid reached USD 8.14 billion in the quarter. Reported net operating income was USD 11.95 billion, up from USD 5.27 billion a year earlier. Equinor attributed the improvement mainly to higher liquid and European gas prices, stronger refining margins and high production.

The board approved a third-quarter cash dividend of USD 0.39 per share. A fourth and final 2026 buyback tranche of up to USD 1.125 billion started on October 29 and is scheduled to run no later than February 1, 2027. The planned 2026 buyback programme totals up to USD 3 billion.

Equinor continued to broaden its energy portfolio during the quarter. The company acquired an interest in the Lackawanna gas-fired power plant in the United States, entered exploration acreage in Namibia and advanced the Bay du Nord project in Canada. Equinor acquired bp's interest in Bay du Nord and sold a 30 percent interest to Shell in October; the project is moving toward an investment decision.

items.t: Burning bridges: Assessing Equinor’s alignment with a 1.5°C pathway
sum: An analysis of Equinor’s contribution to global emissions to date, the impact of planned future oil and gas production, and its compatibility with the remaining global carbon budget and a 1.5°C-aligned pathway

The Norwegian oil major Equinor has significant domestic and international operations. As climate mitigation requirements tighten globally, there is an increasing need to assess the company’s historic and future emissions in relation to a science-based 1.5°C carbon budget.

The purpose of this report is to deliver a comprehensive, data-driven analysis of Equinor’s contribution to global emissions to date and its likely future impact under current and planned expansion pathways.
The report also assesses whether Equinor’s planned developments of new oil and gas fields are compatible with a net zero emissions by 2050 and a 1.5°C of warming by 2100 scenario.

- Equinor has already made a major contribution to global emissions. Since the company was founded as Statoil in 1972, the combustion of oil and gas produced from Equinor’s share of assets has resulted in an estimated 8.66 billion tonnes (Gt) of CO₂ emissions. This is equivalent to more than a fifth of total anthropogenic emissions in 2025.

- Most of these historic emissions come from oil and gas produced in Norway. Emissions from the combustion of oil and gas produced from Norwegian fields accounts for approximately 7.19 GtCO₂ of Equinor’s emissions between 1972 and 2025. This is more than three times Norway’s domestic emissions in the same period, which were 2.08 GtCO₂, and over five times Norway’s per-capita share of past global CO₂ emissions over the same period, at 1.31 GtCO₂.

- Equinor has continued approving new oil and gas projects since the Paris Agreement. In the 10 years since the Paris Agreement up to end of 2025, 64 assets in which Equinor held a stake were approved for development. Equinor invested EUR 28.54 billion in these projects over this period.

items.t: Petrobras buys 50% stake in Equinor’s pre-salt block
sum: Deal in Campos Basin comes as state-run oil company seeks to replenish reserves amid expected pre-salt decline

Petrobras and Norway’s Equinor signed an agreement that will allow the Brazilian state-run oil company to enter the Itaimbezinho block, in the pre-salt area of the Campos Basin, in Rio de Janeiro, through the purchase of a 50% stake in the asset. The value of the deal was not disclosed. The transaction comes as Petrobras seeks to replenish oil reserves amid projections of a decline in pre-salt production.

Equinor held a 100% stake in the block, which it won in the permanent production-sharing offer held by the National Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP) in October 2025. The Norwegian oil company signed the contract for the block on May 27.

In the production-sharing auction, Equinor offered the government 6.95% of profit oil. With the transaction, Equinor and Petrobras will each hold 50% of the block. The Norwegian company will remain the operator of the area. The deal still requires regulatory approvals.

Petrobras said the transaction highlights the importance of activity in Brazil and is aligned with its long-term strategy of replenishing reserves through exploration in new frontiers and partnerships. “The partnership maximizes synergies in the Campos Basin, a region where the company is already developing neighboring assets, also in partnership with Equinor, such as the Raia project and the Jaspe exploratory license,” Petrobras said in a statement.

Equinor, also in a statement, said the partnership maximizes synergies in the Campos Basin, where the company is already developing assets with Petrobras and other oil companies, including the Raia project. “The transaction reinforces the importance of exploration activity for Equinor’s strategy in Brazil.”

In April, Petrobras signed contracts with Malaysia’s Petronas to buy 50% stakes, for $450 million, in the Tartaruga Verde field and Module III of the Espadarte field, both in the Campos Basin. Petrobras then came to hold 100% of both assets.

10 No-Brainer Stocks to Buy as Long as the Strait of Hormuz Is Closed
sum: With the conflict in the Persian Gulf still ongoing, it's a good idea to buy some protection for a portfolio in case of an extended conflict, or even a relatively short one that results in lasting structural damage to the economic activity that preceded it.
Following that line of thought, here's a whistle-stop tour through 10 stocks that can help investors in the current environment.
Three oil stocks to benefit if the price of oil spikes even higher

It's hard not to come across as Captain Obvious here, but oil and gas exploration and production companies are a good place to start, particularly those operating in the U.S., such as Permian Basin-focused Devon Energy (DVN -1.56%) and Diamondback Energy (FANG -0.34%). Those two companies are not only attractive as a tactical way to manage the risk of an oil price spike; they also look like a great value based on the price of oil before the conflict.

The third is integrated major Chevron (CVX -0.15%). Its upstream operations (exploration and production) benefit from a higher price of oil, and its downstream operations (refining) are also benefiting from the widening in the crack spread (difference between crude oil price and refined product price) caused by the difficulty Asian refiners are having obtaining crude oil and the lack of refined product.

Speaking of the crack spread, the most widely followed one is the 3-2-1 spread (the spread between the cost of three barrels of crude and two barrels of gasoline plus one barrel of diesel), and it's blown up to just over $54 from less than $20 at the start of the year.

That's great news for refiners like Valero Energy (VLO -1.36%) and PBF Energy (NYSE: PBF), who source crude from the U.S. regardless of its price. The latter is more of a pure-play refiner (Valero also has a renewable diesel business and ethanol operations), and PBF has outperformed the market. These stocks are likely to outperform as long as the crack spread remains wide and there's no demand destruction for transportation products (gasoline, etc.) caused by high prices.

The risk isn't just a spike in oil prices; there's also a risk that infrastructure damage will be lasting, and that traffic through the Strait of Hormuz could be closed for an extended period. About 20% of the world's energy passes through the Strait of Hormuz, and its closure has severe consequences for the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG), crude oil, and petrochemicals such as urea and fertilizer. The immediate impact will be felt in Asia. The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates that 80% of oil passing through the Strait is destined for Asia, and 90% of LNG, too.

However, if there's a shortage of crude and LNG from the region, Asian countries will compete for energy supplies to Europe, pushing up energy prices for Europeans. items.t: Oil crisis: Are the Poles getting off light?
sum: In Poland there are no signs of fuel panic or dramatic price hikes, even though the government has not introduced emergency measures to protect the market or consumers. The key to this apparent mystery lies in successful diversification.

In recent days the global oil market has once again become extremely volatile. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, security risks affecting maritime transport routes – especially strategic straits – and broader international political conflicts have caused significant fluctuations in oil prices. Such crises typically affect most severely those countries whose energy supply relies heavily on a single supplier or transportation route. Poland, however, has significantly reduced this vulnerability in recent years through a deliberate energy policy, meaning that current disruptions in the oil market are reflected primarily in prices rather than in the security of supply.

The vast majority of Poland’s oil consumption comes from imports. In itself, this would suggest that the country is highly exposed to fluctuations in global markets. Over the past decade, however, one of the key goals of Polish energy policy has been to eliminate one-sided dependencies, particularly on Russian energy resources.
According to an analysis by the International Energy Agency (IEA), diversification of supply sources and the expansion of import routes have become central elements of Poland’s energy strategy.
The report notes that the country has made significant investments in energy infrastructure in recent years, which reduces long-term supply risks.

One of the most visible elements of this strategy was the elimination of Russian oil imports. Poland’s largest energy company, ORLEN, completely stopped purchasing Russian crude by 2025 after the final long-term contract expired.
According to the company’s official statement, this means that all Polish refineries now process crude oil sourced exclusively from non-Russian suppliers.

sum: NEWS ANALYSIS: Oil and gas prices shot up, as did the share prices of many Norwegian companies, after Israel and the US launched their attack on Iran last weekend. Once again, Norway as an oil- and gas-producing nation finds itself benefiting from the sort of military action it otherwise condemns, and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre is calling for the attacks to end.

Støre and his foreign minister, Espen Barth Eide, were quick to criticize the initial attacks on Iran, also the Iranian retaliation not just on Israeli targets but also several other countries in the Middle East. Støre repeated his criticism on national radio Tuesday morning.

“We strongly distance ourselves from the attacks, and that civilians are being hit hard,” Støre said on Norwegian Broadcasting (NRK)’s morning talkshow Politisk kvarter. He also expressed concern over how “the economy, people and civilians are pulled into this.”

Støre believes the US and Israeli attacks on Iran violate the international rule of law. He also criticized Iran’s counter-attacks on several neighbouring countries including the United Arab Emirates, where more than 2,000 Norwegians are among those stranded after airspace closed along with local airports. Some flights were resuming on Thursday, but global aviation has been severely disrupted.

The criticism of Israel’s aggression along with that of the US, long viewed as Norway’s most important ally, sparked strong rebukes from the Israeli Embassy in Oslo. Israel has no ambassador in Norway, but its Chargé d’Affaires Eytan Halon claimed the Norwegians’ criticism was “disappointing” and not rooted in reality. He wondered “which side of history” Norway wants to stand on, and further claimed Norway’s criticism of the attacks launched by the US and Israel differed from other European countries’ views.

Støre and Eide are far from alone in their views, however, and Eide later said he “completely disagreed” with Halon’s assessment. “It’s extremely important for us to try to maintain a world order based on the main principle that no one is allowed to go to war against another country,” Eide told NRK. “You only are allowed to defend yourselves.”

The deposit of USD 335 million paid by PRIO at signing relates to both the 40% and 20% transactions.

"With the closing of this part of the transaction we are handing over operatorship of Peregrino to PRIO and realising significant value for Equinor. The deal is part of our ongoing effort to high-grade our international portfolio, by divesting more mature assets to redeploy capital to assets with greater robustness and more long-term value potential. Brazil remains a core area for Equinor and just last month we started production from Bacalhau, our largest international offshore field, and acquired two exciting exploration blocks in the Campos basin," says Philippe Mathieu, executive vice president for Exploration and Production International at Equinor.

The Peregrino field, located in the Campos Basin east of Rio de Janeiro, has been a cornerstone of Equinor’s international portfolio since production began in 2011. Over the years, the field has produced approximately 300 million barrels of oil and has been a significant contributor to Equinor’s growth in Brazil.

"I want to express gratitude to our employees, partners and suppliers for their contribution to the success of Peregrino over the years. Equinor’s journey in Brazil continues with full momentum with Bacalhau, our Raia gas project, our partnership with Petrobras in Roncador and our growing exploration and renewables portfolio," says Veronica Coelho, senior vice president and country manager for Equinor Brazil.

In May 2025, Equinor also signed a contract for the sale of the remaining 20%, which is subject to certain conditions precedent. Equinor will continue as a non-operated partner until the closing of the remaining 20% share is completed. A further payment is expected at closing of that transaction.
